# ⚡ Kubernetes Command of the Day (2026-08-11)

## 📌 Inspect Pod and Node Resource Utilization

```bash
kubectl top pods --containers
```

| Metadata | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Category** | `Resource-utilization` |
| **Difficulty** | `Beginner` |
| **Safety Rating** | **🟢 Safe** |
| **Verification Status** | Verified ✅ (Verified against cluster with Metrics Server installed.) |

---

### 📖 What It Does

Displays real-time CPU (cores/milli-cores) and Memory (MiB/GiB) consumption per container.

### 💡 Why It Is Useful

Identifies resource hogs, evaluates request/limit accuracy, and pinpoints potential OOM candidates.

### 💻 Practical Example

```bash
kubectl top pods -n default --containers
```

### Command Breakdown

- `top pods`: Fetch live metrics from Metrics Server API.
- `--containers`: Break down metrics per individual container inside multi-container pods.

### ⚙️ Prerequisites

Requires active `kubectl` connection and appropriate cluster permissions.

### ⚠️ Common Mistake

Running against the wrong namespace or context without checking current-context first.
